prompt.context: Our client is a national jewelry retailer that has been experiencing declining profits over the past three years.
prompt.question: Our client has hired us to understand the reason for the decline and provide recommendations on how to improve profitability moving forward.

clarifying_info.q: Have both profit margins and overall profitability declined?
Does the client have a specific profitability target or timeframe?
Any other questions about the situation?
clarifying_info.a: Will get into that later in the case

exhibits.title: Product Mix (%) for the years ended 2010 and 2013
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing product mix percentages across three product lines (Watches, Fashion Jewelry, Wedding & Engagement) for 2010 and 2013. Annual revenues were constant at $1.5M.
exhibits.data: 2010 mix: Watches 30%, Fashion Jewelry 20%, Wedding & Engagement 50%. 2013 mix: Watches 30%, Fashion Jewelry 40%, Wedding & Engagement 30%. Annual revenues constant at $1.5M.

exhibits.title: Unit Contribution Margin (%) for the year ended 2013
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing unit contribution margin percentages for each of the three product lines as of 2013.

framework: Revenue: Price (retail pricing changes, promotions, product mix/segments), Volume (decline in demand, capacity issues)
Costs — Variable: material costs, labor; Fixed: advertising, retail location costs, manufacturing overhead
External — Competition: new entrants, M&A activity, competitive advantages; Customers: change in preferences, price sensitivity; Market: revenue/profitability trends, technology innovations
Great framework also identifies possible recommendations to improve profitability with specific, industry-relevant examples

questions.prompt: Question 1: After looking at Exhibits 1 and 2, calculate the decline in profitability from 2010 to 2013. Note: unit contribution margins have not changed since 2010.
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply revenue ($1.5M) by each product's share of product mix by its contribution margin, sum all three products for each year, then compute the difference. The core insight is that the product mix shifted away from the highest-margin product (Wedding & Engagement) toward the lowest-margin product (Fashion Jewelry), causing the overall profitability decline despite flat revenues.

math.setup: Profitability per product = $1.5M total revenue × product mix % × unit contribution margin %. Sum across all products for each year.
math.answer: Profitability declined by ~$30,000, or approximately 10%, from $292,500 in 2010 to $262,500 in 2013, driven entirely by a shift in product mix toward lower-margin Fashion Jewelry and away from higher-margin Wedding & Engagement.

questions.prompt: Question 2: What recommendations do you have for improving the profitability of each product line?
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers both revenue and cost levers, touches on at least 3 distinct options, and shows industry-specific thinking. Revenue side: volume (new channels such as department stores/online, new customer segments such as US/international/men/women, product extensions) and price (increase prices especially for Fashion Jewelry given its market share growth; avoid price reductions given luxury brand image and already-struggling margins; value-added services like repair). Cost side: interviewer should note that as a luxury provider the client does not believe costs can be reduced. Competition/strategic: focus marketing on Wedding & Engagement given higher profitability and recent decline; diversify into new relevant businesses given market stagnation.

questions.prompt: Question 3: The CEO is thinking about entering the handbag market. How would you approach this question?
questions.guidance: This is a brainstorming question. Candidate should hit at least three considerations and structure the brainstorm (e.g., Internal/External, Opportunities/Threats, Revenue/Cost). Key areas: current handbag market (historic growth/profitability, level of competition); synergies with existing products (capabilities/capacity — can we manufacture?, supplier relationships, handbag experience; brand carryover); entry options (JV/partnership, M&A, organic — note organic is most expensive and time-consuming); financial considerations (can this extension be afforded in short/long term?, are there other projects with better rates of return?).

brainstorming.prompt: The CEO is thinking about entering the handbag market. How would you approach this question?

categories.name: Current Handbag Market
ideas: Historic growth and profitability of the handbag market
Level of competition and key players

categories.name: Synergies with Existing Products
ideas: Capabilities and capacity: can we manufacture handbags? Do we have supplier relationships?
Brand carryover from jewelry to handbags

categories.name: Financial Considerations
ideas: Can this extension be afforded in the short and long term?
Are there other projects on the table with better rates of return?

recommendation: The core issue is a product mix shift: Fashion Jewelry (lowest margin at 10%) grew from 20% to 40% of revenue, while Wedding & Engagement (highest relative margin at 20%) fell from 50% to 30%, causing a ~$30K (10%) profitability decline despite flat revenues
Redirect marketing and sales efforts toward Wedding & Engagement to recover its share of the product mix, given its higher contribution margin
Raise prices on Fashion Jewelry to improve its contribution margin, leveraging its recent market share growth
Explore new channels (online, department stores) and new customer segments to grow total revenue, particularly for Wedding & Engagement
risks: Fashion Jewelry growth may reflect genuine customer preference shifts that are difficult to reverse
Raising prices on Fashion Jewelry could reduce volume and partially offset margin gains
Entering the handbag market requires significant investment and carries execution risk, especially via organic entry
next_steps: Conduct customer research to understand drivers of Fashion Jewelry growth vs. Wedding & Engagement decline
Analyze pricing elasticity for Fashion Jewelry before implementing price increases
Evaluate handbag market entry options more rigorously, prioritizing M&A or JV to minimize cost and time
